source: same verified UNSW IoT Attack Traces and V41 sample protocol
purpose: Fix V41's architectural failure where policy optimization assigned zero weight to the OOD lane. Evaluate independent known-progression and unknown-anomaly lanes whose OR output is calibrated only against benign policy traffic.
claim_scope: unseen-family early progression forecasting after the first observable malicious network change; not prediction before the first malicious packet
sample_protocol: identical to V41: 4 one-minute rows, 240-second continuation target, 30-minute device-time block split, locked-family exclusion

representation.environment_normalization: per-device robust median/IQR fitted on benign TRAIN blocks only; device identity is not a model feature
representation.supervised_lane: HGB trained on non-heldout known progression positives plus benign samples
representation.unknown_lane: composite benign novelty: IsolationForest percentile plus robust onset-shock percentile; no attack labels used to fit the anomaly reference

decision_policy.calibration: supervised logit calibration on calibration split only; anomaly empirical references use benign calibration samples only
decision_policy.budget_pair_meaning: [supervised benign FPR budget, unknown-lane benign FPR budget]
decision_policy.selection: choose the first predeclared pair whose combined OR alert has <=1.05% benign FPR on policy data; attack-positive policy outcomes are not used to choose the pair

final_validation: locked; V42 is development evidence only and newly reserved external validation is required before a final zero-day-like claim
